claims.text: As-deposited high-entropy-alloy bond coats exhibit heterogeneous, underdeveloped oxide scales with limited protective properties.
A controlled pre-oxidation anneal in an oxygen-containing atmosphere will generate a continuous, thin, alumina-rich passivating scale.
The scale produced by pre-oxidation will be uniform and coherent.
The pre-formed alumina-rich scale acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The oxygen diffusion barrier reduces subsequent oxidation.
The pre-formed alumina-rich scale reduces subsequent oxide-scale growth.
The pre-formed alumina-rich scale mitigates spallation.
Mitigating oxidation and spallation improves adhesion between the bond coat and ceramic top coat under cyclic thermal stress.
Pre-oxidized bond coats will exhibit less oxidation-driven degradation than untreated bond coats.
Pre-oxidized bond coats will show delayed spallation relative to untreated bond coats.
Controlled pre-oxidation will improve bond-coat durability and extend service life relative to an untreated baseline.
The beneficial effect should persist under high-temperature cyclic oxidation conditions typical of thermal-barrier-coating service.
The beneficial effect depends on the alloy composition supporting alumina formation without detrimental phase changes.
Excessive pre-oxidation scale growth or phase instability can eliminate the beneficial effect.
The beneficial effect is limited to service conditions within the thermal-stability range of the formed scale.
